text: Carries the full content for all 25 prompts and is by far the cheapest to produce: about 1,600 characters at the median. It never interacts. Charts become block characters, checklists cannot be ticked, and all seven input tasks turn into a list of questions plus a template to fill in, so they need at least one more message.
a2ui: Cards, tabs and data-bound lists structure answers well, and forms are a strength: checks hold the submit button back until the input is valid, then one event carries the bound values to the agent. The basic catalog has no table, chart, arithmetic, client-side filtering or conditional visibility. So tables are weighted rows, bars are block characters, and anything that recomputes (the interest, car-cost and bill calculators) or filters (the directory and the flight list) needs an agent round trip.
html: The most expressive rendering for every prompt: real charts, a sequence diagram, a sorting race, drag and drop, live calculators and forms that reveal fields as you answer. The price is size (about 8,500 characters at the median, five times the text answer), a different visual style on every page, and isolation. Inside an allow-scripts sandbox with no network there is nowhere to keep state or send a result, so all seven input tasks end on the page.
agui: Strongest where the job is to hand structured data back. For the seven input tasks and the incident decision it returns a typed result validated against the tool call's output schema, with rules that show or enable fields. It is weakest as a display: 18 of the 25 prompts fall back on a read-only table of disabled inputs under a one-line label, and a form has no charts, no computed values and no live filtering.
